import subprocess


def make(argv):
    def run():
        subprocess.run(argv)
    return run


argv = ["pacman", "-S", "r22-missing-required"]
runner = make()
runner()
rationale: Python 3.14.8 call semantics make this decidable rather than uncertain. 'runner = make()' calls 'make' with zero arguments. 'make' declares one required positional parameter 'argv' with no default. A call always assigns a value to every declared parameter, from positional arguments, keyword arguments, or default values; here none of the three sources can supply 'argv', so argument binding raises TypeError before the body of 'make' executes. No except clause is present anywhere in the cell, so the exception propagates out of the statement and out of the transcript: 'runner' is never bound and 'runner()' is unreachable. Even if the nested function object 'run' were somehow formed, it would carry 'argv' as a free variable bound to 'make''s parameter cell, and that parameter never received a value; it could not resolve to the module-level 'argv'. Because 'subprocess.run(argv)' sits only inside the never-entered body of 'run', the transcript provably spawns no process. The single precise static truth is therefore zero findings (no-findings with a source reason): any row naming 'pacman -S r22-missing-required' would fabricate an observed execution by lending the same-named module global into a closure whose required parameter was never bound -- the F2 defect family. A lead row would also be wrong, because the body is provably unreachable rather than unresolved-but-reachable; a lead asserts a possible spawn, and this transcript has none. Nothing in the cell is unparseable, and the make() call is not an unbound-argument case like make(*parts) whose outcome is unknowable: its arity failure is visible in the source, so 'uncertain' is not the honest label. Truth is static only; no payload was executed.
